title: Southwest Virginia Museum Historical State Park to offer 'Creepy Cryptids' and more programs Oct. 24

content:
BIG STONE GAP, Va. (WJHL) — The Southwest Virginia Museum Historical State Park is hosting a slate of spooky-themed programs, including a Creepy Cryptids event, on Oct. 24.

According to a news release from the park, the events are free to attend, and registration isn't required. All programs are family-friendly. The Southwest Virginia Museum Historical State Park is located at 10 W 1st Street N in Big Stone Gap.

 Lincoln Theatre to celebrate Halloween through various shows 

The following events will take place at the museum on Oct. 24:

Creepy Cryptids

  • Oct. 24, noon-1 p.m.

  • Victorian Parlor inside the museum

  • Join park rangers and volunteers for a deep dive into some of southern Appalachia's most intriguing legends and local mysteries, from Norton's famous Woodbooger to the 1987 UFO sightings over Wytheville

Discovering the Symbolism of Historic Gravestones

  • Oct. 24, 2-3 p.m.

  • Victorian Parlor inside the museum

  • Learn about the symbols carved into historic gravestones and what they reveal about the lives, beliefs and traditions of past generations

A Stroll Through Glencoe Historic Cemetery

  • Oct. 24, 5-6 p.m.

  • Glencoe Cemetery

  • Uncover stories of some of the town's most memorable figures

  • Please wear comfortable shoes and be prepared for moderate standing and walking

More information on the events taking place this month at the park can be found by calling 276-523-9640 or going online to dcr.virginia.gov/state-parks/southwest-virginia-museum.

The Southwest Virginia Museum is an 1890s Victorian stone mansion with an original oak interior; it's a National Historic Landmark. The museum's collection includes more than 60,000 pieces and state-of-the-art exhibits that tell the story of the region's exploration and development from the pioneer era to the mining "boom and bust" of the late 1800s.
